messages:
ops-bot: P1 created — serving runtime cluster experiencing repeated CUDA_ILLEGAL_DEVICE_ADDRESS crashes on gpu-node-7 (gpu-pool-4). Auto-evacuation triggered, 3 container restarts in last 6m. Creating channel for triage. :fire:

Maya (oncall): seeing the alert flood. rate: ~80 errors/min for /v1/generate on models/large-quant. Started correlating with a rolling kernel/module push ~40m ago.

Sam (sre): confirmed node flapping: kubelet restarted containers, OOM not reported in kube - containers crash with SIGSEGV in runtime. Nodes showing dmesg device faults. Putting a cordon on gpu-node-7 now.

Sam (sre): `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Eli (eng-runtime): pinging in — saw a brief spike in nvml/Xid 31 yesterday in staging; could be an nv driver/kernel module mismatch with our fast restart path. Can we get dmesg and a crash log from one container?

Maya (oncall): grabbing dmesg and container logs. attaching snippets below.

Maya (oncall): ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, Ch 00000010, Intr 10000000. ILA: 0x7f8a3c000000, PID: 8421, GPU:0
[ 1234.568200] RIP: 0010:0x7f8a3c000128
[ 1234.568300] ---[ end trace 9f5a1b2c3d4e5f ]---
[ 1234.569000] kernel: invalid read of device-mapped address 0x7f8a3c000000 by process model-server (pid 8421)
```

Maya (oncall): container stderr: ```
runtime: cuda: illegal memory access
stack: 0x55a1b2c3
...
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): kvcache: misaligned pointer during restore
```

Eli (eng-runtime): that "misaligned pointer during restore" string rings a bell — likely when we hydrate KV cache pages on hot-start the pinned GPU pointer alignment differs due to a kernel module's changed dma_alloc behavior after the driver update. Not typical OOM.

Grace (prod): customer impact: we’re seeing ~0.5% error rate for hosted production traffic, some enterprise customers on dedicated pools may have retries and increased latency. No broad data loss. Notifying CS to prepare customer messages.

Mike (support): prepping notification draft. cc @Grace :eyes:

Sam (sre): mitigation options: 1) evacuate affected nodes (done), 2) roll back kernel/driver across pool, 3) disable KV cache restore during container start (runtime change) to avoid misaligned pinned mappings, 4) force software fallback to CPU for affected models. Which do we want to pursue short-term?

Eli (eng-runtime): short-term: push runtime env var to disable fast-kv-restore on deployments in gpu-pool-4: `ML_RUNTIME_FAST_KV_RESTORE=0` then restart pods. That avoids the aligned pinned pointer path. Longer: revert the driver/kernel push or coordinate with infra for a proper driver ABI shim.

Maya (oncall): starting a canary update for the runtime config on one node in gpu-pool-4 (model-gen-canary).

deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-config-update to model-gen-canary (1/1) by Eli (eng-runtime) — https://ci/release/3982 :rocket:

Eli (eng-runtime): applied env var and restarted pod on gpu-node-9 (canary). Monitoring logs.

Maya (oncall): canary logs show no cuda illegal errors in last 5m. Good sign. Rolling to remaining nodes in gpu-pool-4, doing 1 node at a time.

Sam (sre): draining additional nodes as we roll, keeping capacity headroom > 20%. If we see reappearance we’ll fallback to CPU route.

Maya (oncall): roll underway. Current status: 3/6 nodes patched, error rate dropped from 80/min to ~6/min cluster-wide.

Grace (prod): CS: sending a short-status to impacted customers: "Intermittent GPU errors causing retries, mitigation in progress, per-route impact ~0.5% errors, no data corruption." Drafted and queued.

Eli (eng-runtime): adding a temporary runtime guard: on KV restore verify dma_alloc alignment and if misaligned allocate a new aligned buffer in GPU-visible memory and memcpy. Patching now (fast patch, not optimal).

Eli (eng-runtime): patch applied to canary. logs show restore path using fallback allocation and no crashes. Planning broader rollout after smoke.

Sam (sre): executing slow-roll: patch env var + runtime patch to remaining nodes. Doing 1 node every 3m.

Maya (oncall): update: last_message_ts 1758887400 — roll complete. Error rate back to baseline (<0.01%). All previously cordoned nodes rejoined.

Grace (prod): customer message sent, CS inbound tickets created for enterprise accounts with high retry rates.

Mike (support): closing immediate alerts; creating follow-up ticket for postmortem and RCA.

Eli (eng-runtime): postmortem TODOs: 1) full root-cause: confirm driver/kernel change that altered dma alignment semantics; 2) permanent fix: robust KV restore that never depends on driver alignment or use pinned allocations with explicit alignment; 3) add runtime health check to detect misaligned restores early; 4) add automated fallback to CPU when Xid 31 spikes.

Sam (sre): infrastructure TODO: coordinate with infra team to evaluate the kernel/driver rollout and decide whether to roll back or publish a compatibility shim.

Maya (oncall): handing off to Eli and Sam for next 24h follow-up. I’ll update the incident ticket (INC-2026-043) with timeline and mitigation steps. If anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:

Eli (eng-runtime): acknowledged — will own RCA + runtime fix.

Sam (sre): acknowledged — will own infra coordination and rollback plan if needed.

ops-bot: Incident P1 resolved (mitigated) — error rate returned to baseline and customers notified. Follow-up tasks assigned in INC-2026-043. :white_check_mark:
